title: Derived tensor and actual pullback tensor arrows under section equivalence
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and take their small pro-étale sites small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], also writing $R_T$ for its reconstructed section-ring sheaf. Let $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the fixed equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary module operations, their specified adjunctions, and geometric composition comparisons of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Use the signed direct-sum totals, K-flat complexes and derived relative tensors of [pur713-def-kflat-module, def-pc-kflat-complex, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], the derived operation comparisons of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] and the ordinary tensor normalization of [lem-pd-section-ordinary-oplax-normalization]. The induced equivalence $D(E_T)$ identifies internal derived relative tensor with the canonical ringed K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], with its localization comparison and regular-module unit. For all derived internal $R_Y$-modules $M,N$, under these comparisons the actual derived oplax arrow $\delta_f:Lf^*(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)\to Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*N$ induced by internal pullback and localization equals the canonical ringed tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The actual internal lax arrow $\mu_f=\delta_f^{-1}$ equals its inverse. These are equalities of specified natural transformations, compatible with their tensor-unit and constraint comparisons.

proof.text: The chosen qTensor satisfies TensorRepresentativeCondition by tensor_representatives. The K-flat section comparison supplies the specified oplax structure on the section equivalence, with tensor component theta and identity unit. Its oplax associativity and unitor axioms give exactly the equivalence constraint equations.

Conjugate the actual internal delta by the fixed section equivalence, theta, gamma, and the equivalence counits to obtain a natural isomorphism on section-derived tensor pairs. Restriction to flat-term K-flat representatives is injective by site derived tensor descent. On those representatives the actual representative square identifies its composite with the output comparison with the defining cochain path of tensorPullComparison. Cancel the invertible output comparison. Thus the conjugated actual isomorphism equals tensorPullComparison. Identify totalPullComparison with the forward map of sectionTotalIso using the proved forward-projection API of [def-pd-section-total-oplax-comparison-data], and simplify the reflexive eqToHom transports. This retains the prescribed total map while avoiding expansion of the complete tensor isomorphism.

Whisker the desired internal comparison square by the product of the inverse section equivalence, which is fully faithful. Substitute the equality of conjugated isomorphisms from the previous step. Naturality and the inverse equations for theta, gamma and the equivalence counits cancel the extra outer factors. Equality of the inverse natural isomorphisms gives the stated lax comparison square as well.

Multiply the actual representative unit equation on the left by gamma and the image of the regular-unit comparison, and on the right by the inverse regular-unit comparison. Cancel inverse pairs. The representative regular comparison is exactly normalizationDerivedRegularUnit; functoriality of the degree-zero single-complex functor identifies the remaining composite with normalizationDerivedSectionUnit.

Use the existing generic leftDerivedMonoidalWithUnit construction: its tensor component is precisely internalDelta. The proved equality of the adjunction-mate ordinary oplax structure with the canonical scalar-extension structure identifies its unit with normalizationDerivedInternalUnit. Transport this oplax structure across the two strong section equivalences and gamma using the proved OplaxMonoidal.ofLaxSquare construction. The tensor square identifies the resulting tensor component with tensorPullComparison, and the unit equation identifies its unit with normalizationDerivedSectionUnit. Its associativity and two unitality axioms are the remaining three equations. These are generic monoidal/localization tools; no additional representative computation is needed.
